name: Autarky
scope: Autarky is economic self-sufficiency, applied to a state, community or economic system. Britannica (s2) defines it as 'an economic system of self-sufficiency and limited trade', complete when a country has a closed economy with no international trade, and gives mercantilist Europe, Nazi Germany's bloc economy and North Korea's juche as historical or extreme cases; the New Palgrave entry (s3) treats it both as a theoretical construct in trade theory and as a policy of economic self-sufficiency, and INOMICS (s4) adds that it can be pursued in strategic fields such as energy and that populist trade-barrier platforms draw on it. The scope here is the policy doctrine of national (or regional) economic self-sufficiency and closing the economy to foreign trade, from the complete form to partial or sectoral forms, with its stated purposes (security, planning, peace, independence from foreign economic pressure). Its earliest worked-out blueprint is Fichte's The Closed Commercial State (s5, s7), which the study of economic nationalism published by the Mises Institute (s5) presents as a collectivist plan for a state sealed off from foreign trade under state control of trade and a national currency; Nazi Germany's Four Year Plan treated autarky as a short-term aim to prepare for war, though Hitler held that it could not last (s6). India's Third Plan (s8) is kept as an adjacent programme: it calls for a 'self-reliant economy' but says self-reliance 'does not mean a search for self-sufficiency', so only its self-reliance aims, not complete self-sufficiency, count for the subject. Excluded: the Stoic and Epicurean ethical autarkeia of the individual, 'economic independence' as personal financial independence of women, families or the poor (the books on welfare and women's economic independence), and the economists' defence of free trade, which counts only as the critics' side (they show it is a set of ideas, never what it holds).

common-currency.rationale: Fichte's closing of the commercial state rests on replacing world money with a national currency valid only inside the state (Closed Commercial State, preface; Heilperin Chapter V, section V), which a currency shared across countries would undo; the scholarly definitions are silent on money.

free-trade.rationale: Britannica calls autarkic systems 'the opposite of liberal economic systems, which encourage the free flow of goods and services', and Fichte, in Heilperin's account of The Closed Commercial State, calls demands for free trade undesirable and harmful.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: In Heilperin's account (Chapter V, section III), Fichte makes trade the major cause of war between states and closes the commercial state in the interest of peace, the opposite of the statement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: India's Third Plan makes self-reliance its aim: an economy 'more and more able out of its own resources to pay for its own development' with dependence on foreign aid shrinking (chapter 'The Conquest of Poverty', p. 20-21), while still accepting aid for the time being and rejecting complete self-sufficiency.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: INOMICS says autarkic arguments, central to populist platforms, call for trade barriers and domestic protections to support local industries, and that some autarkic policy may be called for; Fichte goes beyond tariffs to a state trade monopoly, so support is modest.

summary: Autarky is the policy or condition of economic self-sufficiency: a state, community or economy that produces what it needs and limits or ends trade with others. Defined as the opposite of free-trade liberalism, it ranges from a fully closed economy to partial self-sufficiency in strategic goods, and its sources are about economics rather than a full social programme. Its defining texts say little about most political questions, so only trade, currency and self-reliance statements are answered.

missingStatements.text: A country should aim to produce at home what it needs rather than rely on imports.
missingStatements.rationale: Self-sufficiency in production and limited trade is what the definitions of autarky describe (Britannica, INOMICS).

quotes.text: Autarky is an economic system of self-sufficiency and limited trade.
They would refuse international trade and only consume goods produced within the country.

notes: Themes searched: trade, tariffs, money, planning, aid, peace and war, alliances, immigration, local production, in the defining sources (Britannica, New Palgrave abstract, INOMICS, Heilperin on Fichte, Evans) and in the downloaded books. Most of the downloaded books use 'economic independence' for personal or household independence (welfare hearings, women, GAO), the Frejlich and Arab books were not tied to the scope, and the Fichte and Massachusetts books are philosophy and adult education, so only India's Third Plan (s8) answers. The sources define autarky economically and take few positions on government, society or culture, so nearly every statement is null. The India plan rejects self-sufficiency, so only its self-reliance aims are used.
